trust_decision.summary: Whether a request that never completes the WebSocket handshake may keep its waiter is decided by who clears the waiter registry: only the wss 'connection' callback and the post-fetch waiter check clear it, and neither runs when the handshake is aborted.

landing_point.why: The advisory is about an aborted handshake, and the server 'upgrade' listener is the only place that decides what happens to an upgrade that never reaches 'connection' (400 response, response headers, wss.handleUpgrade).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Calling upgradeWebSocket twice for one request (middleware plus route, or parent app plus mounted sub-app) is an unsupported way to use the helper, so the waiter it silently overwrites is not a real case.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Coexistence with a second 'upgrade' listener and with concurrent handshakes on the shared wss: a rejection response may only be written when the adapter is the sole listener, and each request keeps its own waiter, so a fix that rejects or clears on any socket close, or writes a response from the new cleanup path, breaks the 'should not block other upgrade listeners' case (test/websocket.test.ts:139-164) and in-flight handshakes of other clients.

O6_input_shapes: aborted handshake with an invalid Sec-WebSocket-Key (the report's example and the shape of the added test, fix.diff:97-139)
handshake rejected by ws for other header reasons (missing key, unsupported Sec-WebSocket-Version, non-GET) - the same socket 'close' path settles it (fix.diff:56-58)
socket closed or errored while the fetch callback is still resolving, when the close event arrives after the reclaimer is attached (src/websocket.ts:203-219 vs fix.diff:58)
upgrade request whose route never registered a waiter, which must still get the 400/401 rejection (src/websocket.ts:221-229)

O7_producer.where: src/websocket.ts:266-268 (waiter registered through waitForWebSocket at src/websocket.ts:185-189)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client closes the TCP connection while the fetch callback is still awaiting: by the time the fix's 'close' reclaimer is attached the socket is already destroyed and its 'close' event has already fired, so nothing settles the waiter and wss.handleUpgrade then finds no waiter callback to run
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The peer already closed the connection, so the handshake is finished and the request is garbage that will be collected - only live-socket aborts like the report's need handling.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same listener, ~25 lines above the fix's attach point (fix.diff:58)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The user-supplied fetch callback throws (or rejects) after upgradeWebSocket has registered the waiter: the catch returns before the reclaimer is attached, so the waiter entry is never removed
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A throwing fetch is a 500/abort error path, not a WebSocket path; the socket is ended in the same branch, so there is nothing to reclaim and the request is considered finished.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same listener, ~30 lines above the fix's attach point (fix.diff:58)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A second upgradeWebSocket call for the same request (middleware plus route, or parent app plus mounted sub-app) overwrites the single waiterMap entry: the first promise is unreachable and can never be settled, so its pending async closure keeps the IncomingMessage alive for the process lifetime even with the published fix, whose rejectWaiter only settles the entry currently in the map
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The helper is documented for one route (README.md:70-94); registering it twice on one request is a misuse/unsupported combination, not a supported route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different closure: registration in the per-route helper (src/websocket.ts:266-268), cleanup in the server's upgrade listener

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second keyed registry for in-flight upgrades (a handshake-timeout map, or a per-request map of response headers to append) that needs the same settle-on-close cleanup
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already keys pending work by IncomingMessage and carries per-upgrade state on symbol-keyed env fields (src/websocket.ts:91-100); adding a handshake timeout or per-request header tracking would naturally add another entry with the same lifecycle and the same missing cleanup.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-request registry of close handlers or abort controllers, released only when the response finishes or the outgoing stream closes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Cleanup on this path hangs off outgoing.on('close') (src/listener.ts:386, handler at src/listener.ts:89-115), and upgrade requests deliberately have no outgoing (src/websocket.ts:96 sets outgoing: undefined), so any request-keyed registry built on this pattern leaks every aborted upgrade - the existing 'Memory leak test' suite (test/server.test.ts:1106-1174) shows the maintainers already test exactly this property on the normal path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A module-level Map<IncomingMessage, Promise> body-read cache instead of the per-request bodyReadPromiseKey (src/request.ts:553), retaining the request whenever the reader never settles
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Body recovery after client disconnect (#375) already caches per-request read state on the incoming object; hoisting it to a map shared between the listener and the upgrade path is a plausible deduplication refactor that reintroduces the same retention bug.

O9_family: memory leak / unbounded retention of per-request state (CWE-401, CWE-770) leading to unauthenticated denial of service

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a reject to the waiter and call it from the existing waiterMap.delete branch at src/websocket.ts:223-229, i.e. clean up only where the code already deletes - a branch that never runs for an aborted handshake.

out_of_scope_notes: Upgrade requests bypass getRequestListener entirely (src/server.ts:21 passes the raw options.fetch to setupWebSocket), so autoCleanupIncoming and the custom errorHandler never apply to them; that is a different protection from this advisory and was not pursued.
unverified: ws internals were not inspected (no node_modules in the pinned tree), so which abort paths in ws 8.x return from handleUpgrade without invoking its callback is inferred from the advisory and from the fix's close-listener design rather than read in the library.
